subject: Operations
title: Nike's Supply Chain Stumble
description: Learn Nike's Supply Chain Stumble in one minute.

hook.text: Nike's demand planning software miscalculated. Too many slow sellers, not enough best sellers. Cost: $100 million.

buildup.text: In 2001, Nike deployed i2's demand planning software to forecast what shoes to produce and in what quantities.

discovery.text: The software generated wildly wrong forecasts—overestimating unpopular shoes and underestimating popular ones.

twist.text: Nike blamed the software. i2 blamed the implementation. The real failure was deploying without proper testing.

climax.text: Nike lost $100 million in sales, its stock dropped 20%, and the CEO acknowledged the technology fumble publicly.

punchline.text: Bad software forecasts make expensive shoes nobody buys.

quiz.question: What went wrong with Nike's demand planning software?
